data.one_liner: Runtime application self-protection for Flutter to detect root, emulators, debuggers, and SSL pinning.
data.what_it_does: Detects runtime tampering including root, jailbreak, emulators, debuggers, hooks, and VPNs on Android and iOS. Provides SSL certificate pinning, screen capture protection, and a built-in security reporting client.
use_when: You need to protect a high-security financial or enterprise app from rooted or modified devices.
You require SSL certificate pinning to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.
You need to ship security telemetry and threat events back to your own backend.
avoid_when: Your application does not handle sensitive user or enterprise data requiring anti-tampering measures.
You are targeting platforms other than Android and iOS.
strengths: Detects 16 different threats across Android and iOS.
Includes built-in SSL certificate pinning supporting local and remote certificates.
Offers automatic or manual encrypted local queueing for security reports sent to your backend.
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific configuration and Swift Package Manager for iOS.
Some detection mechanisms might cause false positives on heavily customized or developer devices.
data.setup_notes: Requires Android API 24+ and iOS 15.0+ with Swift Package Manager enabled. Configuration requires specifying team IDs, bundle IDs, and signing certificate hashes.
